messages.subject: QUERY: Multi-species design in Distance
parts:
--Original Message Text---
From: BSPB
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 1999 10:46:44 +0300

Hello,
My name is Boris Barov and I am new in DISTANCE. I conduct a point count
survey in
oak-pseudomaquise scrub investigating bird communities. I stratified my
observations by habitat type on the basis of structural differences in
vegetation
cover (the study area is exteremely patchy). However, I would like to know
whether
it is possible to post-stratify by species (the species composition of my
communies is of 21 species). Or maybe I should compose separate DISTANCE
project
for each species? Which is the approach recommended by DISTANCE? I am aware
that
poststratification capabilities of DISTANCE 3.5 are limited.
Hope to hear from you soon.

Yours,
Boris Barov, BSPB\BirdLife Bulgaria
--------------------------

Boris,

Your question is quite a common one, so I have sent my reply to the distance-
sampling email list as well as to you (see the "Email list" link on
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/ if you don't know about the list).

In version 3.5 of Distance you can only stratify by one level at once. So
you can either stratify by habitat type or by species. However, in your case
this is not a major problem since you presumably do not wish to estimate a
combined density of "birds" over all species - instead you probably want to
estimate the density of each species separately. In this case, set up your
project with habitat type as the stratum layer, and species name as an extra
field in the observation layer. Then create one Data Filter for each species
you wish to analyze. In each Data Filter, use the Data Selection tab to
include only data for that species -- for example for Robins your data filter
would include only data where layer name is "Observation", field name is
"Species", operator is "=" and value is "Robin". To analyze data for the
Robin, you would then pair up this Data Filter with the Model Definition of
your choice. (In the Model Definition, under Stratum Definition on the
Estimate tab you would choose the "Use stratum layer" option to stratify by
habitat.)

The alternative you suggest, using a separate project file for each species,
will also work fine. The down side of this, however, is that you cannot
share Model Definitions among projects, so you would have to set these up
separately in each project.

Good luck with your analysis. All the best,

- Len Thomas
